title: ر/ل, and long vs short vowels

bigIdea.text: Two last contrasts. ر is one quick tap of the tongue tip; ل is a clear 'l' that touches and holds. And vowel length matters: a short vowel lasts one count, a long one two. Get the length wrong and you can change the word.

proper.text: Places: ل is made with the front edges of the tongue against the upper teeth, on one or both sides. ر is made with the tip of the tongue, toward its top, at the roots of the upper front teeth.

How they differ: for ل the tongue touches and stays while the sound flows out around its sides; for ر the tip gives one quick tap and lets go, so keep its repetition small. ل is light (except in the word Allah after a fatha or damma); ر is heavy with a fatha or damma and light with a kasra. English speakers: avoid the curled English 'r' and the dark 'l' of 'ball'.
Sifat: both are 'in between' (tawassut), both hold the breath back (jahr), and both 'lean' (inhiraf). Only ر has 'repetition' (takrir: the tongue tip can vibrate).

proper.text: Vowel length: Arabic has three short vowels (a, i, u) and three matching long ones (aa, ii, uu), and length is part of the word.

Counting: a short vowel (fatha, kasra or damma) lasts one count. A vowel followed by its madd letter (ا after a fatha, و after a damma, ي after a kasra) lasts two counts: the natural madd. Common mistakes: English speakers clip long vowels and stretch short ones; Persian readers let kasra drift to 'e' and damma to 'o'.

memoryHook.text: Ra taps, lam holds; one count short, two counts long.

extras.text: Tap a steady beat with one finger: one tap for a short vowel, two taps for a long one. Keep every count the same length.

tip.text: ل: the tongue touches and stays; the sound flows around its sides. ر: one quick tap with the tip, and the tongue lets go at once.
Same 'a', different length: بَ is one count, بَا is two. Do not change the vowel, only hold it.
Same 'i', different length: one count, then two. Keep it a clear 'i', not 'e'.
Same 'u', different length: one count, then two. Keep it a clear 'u', not 'o'.

explain: Right: alif after a fatha, waw after a damma, ya after a kasra.
